text:
Davish

 A desktop for your Linux servers. 
Terminal, files, services, Docker, logs, cron, nginx, ports, a browser, disk, login security, SSH keys, packages and git over plain SSH, in one place that feels like an operating system. 
Nothing to install on the server.

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 English · Tiếng Việt · 简体中文 · davish.app 

 
 
 

 

 Why Davish

- Open it and you're in. No login screen, no web panel: Davish connects to the server you used last with your SSH key and puts you on its desktop. Nothing extra listens on the server, so there is no new port to open or protect.
- Agentless. Davish only needs sshd and SFTP. Everything runs from your machine over SSH; nothing is copied to, installed on or left behind on the server.
- You see every command. Anything destructive (stop a service, remove a file, restart a container, replace a crontab) shows the exact command before it runs. The command log records everything Davish ran on your behalf, and exports the changes as a shell script you can read and run again.
- Secrets stay in your keychain. Passwords and passphrases live only in the OS keychain. A sudo password is never saved: when root is needed, Davish asks for it once per session, keeps it in memory only, forgets it after 15 minutes unused and hands it to sudo on stdin, or you run the command in a terminal yourself.
- Locks when you step away. A lock password of its own, Touch ID on macOS; it locks when the machine wakes, after idle time or with ⌘L . Sessions keep running behind the lock, but nothing reaches a server until you unlock.
- Many servers, one desktop. Each server is a workspace ( ⌘1 … ⌘9 ) that remembers its own windows. Copy files between servers by dragging them. Give a server a tag ( prod , staging …) and a group, so a red prod stays on screen and servers sit in folders.
- Updates itself. A new version shows its changes with Update, Later and Skip this version; Davish downloads it, checks its signature and restarts into it. No reinstalling.
- English, Vietnamese, Simplified Chinese or Spanish. Pick the language in Settings; the first time, Davish follows your system's. Spanish is new: corrections are welcome in 124.
- Your /.ssh/config works, and so does your Ansible inventory. Import their hosts in one go, keys and ProxyJump included, a whole Ansible group at a time; Davish only reads the files. Servers behind a bastion connect through it, each hop with its own host key check, and the whole chain reconnects on its own.

 Features

 On the server 

- Terminal: tabs, GPU rendering, color schemes, an optional powerline prompt
- Saved commands: your frequent commands, typed into Terminal in one click
- Command log: every command Davish ran, exported as a script that runs the changes again over ssh
- Files: Finder-style SFTP, drag and drop, copy between servers, search names and contents on the server, hold a file for a ring of actions
- Editor: CodeMirror with atomic saves, backups and options
- Logs: journal, files and containers, live, and search their whole history on the server
- Monitor: CPU, memory, disks, network, GPUs, processes, on Linux and Windows servers
- All servers: every server's health and alerts in one window, in folders by group and filtered by state, group or tag, a map of what each one serves, and one command run on several servers, a terminal tab each

 Services and apps 

- Services: systemd units, status, journal
- Docker: one card per compose project (or a table), images and layers, volumes
- Cron: schedules in plain words
- Nginx: sites, nginx -t before reload, TLS expiry
- Packages: updates with security fixes first, runtimes; one-click install command when Docker, nginx, git or a database is missing
- Database: MariaDB/MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB and SQLite; find, create, dump and restore, read SQLite tables, MongoDB login kept in the keychain
- Git: status, diffs, commit graph, fetch and pull
- Shortcuts: drag deploy.sh onto the desktop, double-click to run, with a stop button

 Network and security 

- Ports & tunnels: listening ports, tunnels to 127.0.0.1 
- Browser: open the server's localhost:3000 inside Davish
- Disk: where the space goes as a tree, what could not be measured and why, delete and clean up
- Security: failed logins per hour and by address, users targeted, open sessions, ufw, fail2ban
- SSH keys: authorized keys, deploy keys, your own keys
- /.ssh/config, Ansible and ProxyJump: import hosts from ssh config or an INI inventory, connect through a bastion

 The desktop 

- Spotlight & Launchpad: open anything with ⌘K , every app by group
- Menu bar and help: every command and shortcut, a ? on each app, and your choice of what opens at start
- App lock: Touch ID or a password, locks on wake
- Updates: one click to a new version, signature checked
- Light and dark: follows your system, or pick one
- Language: English, Vietnamese, Simplified Chinese or Spanish

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Every app in detail, with screenshots → 

 Screenshots show demo data from the browser preview.

 Install

Prebuilt apps for macOS (universal), Windows and Linux are attached to each release.

- macOS 12 or later. Open Davish-…-macos-universal.pkg to install into Applications. The app is not signed yet, so macOS blocks it the first time: click Done , open System Settings → Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway next to the line about Davish (again for Davish.app if it is blocked). Or run xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine on the file.
- Windows 10 or later. Run Davish-…-windows-amd64-setup.exe ; it installs the WebView2 runtime if it is missing. Windows SmartScreen may warn about an unknown publisher: choose More info → Run anyway .

install.title: Install
install.html:
Prebuilt apps for macOS (universal), Windows and Linux are attached to each release.

  • macOS 12 or later. Open Davish-…-macos-universal.pkg to install into Applications. The app is not signed yet, so macOS blocks it the first time: click Done, open System Settings → Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway next to the line about Davish (again for Davish.app if it is blocked). Or run xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine on the file.
  • Windows 10 or later. Run Davish-…-windows-amd64-setup.exe; it installs the WebView2 runtime if it is missing. Windows SmartScreen may warn about an unknown publisher: choose More info → Run anyway.
  • Linux with GTK 3 and WebKitGTK 4.1. The window is drawn on the GPU, WebKitGTK's own default, except on the proprietary NVIDIA driver, where it stays off until it has been tested: start Davish with DAVISH_WEBVIEW_GPU=always to try it (Davish then sets WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1, the usual fix for a blank window there, unless you set it yourself) and tell us how it went in #185. If the window stays blank or flickers on any machine, start it with DAVISH_WEBVIEW_GPU=never; the app log (~/.cache/davish/logs) has a linux webview gpu line saying what was chosen and why.
What the server needs
Feature Requirement
Everything OpenSSH server with the SFTP subsystem
Services, Logs (journal) systemd; to read system logs, a user in the adm or systemd-journal group
Docker the docker CLI; a user in the docker group (Davish offers the install command when it is missing)
Cron crontab
Nginx nginx with sites-available / sites-enabled or conf.d

Actions that need root (stopping a system service, editing a root-owned file) show the exact command first, then run through sudo with the password asked once per session, or go to a terminal with sudo typed in. Nothing runs as root silently, and what could lock you out of the server stays in the terminal.
